# T001 criterion inventory — proposed test case design

This is a **design inventory**, not an executed test report, application implementation, or final `docs/sdlc` deliverable. It crosswalks every approved REQ-001–REQ-024 acceptance criterion to approved implementation TASK-001–TASK-006. TC-001–TC-024 are proposed identifiers, not existing tests. `TASK-005` denotes the proposed pytest suite in addition to the task responsible for behavior; `TASK-006` denotes documentation/audit. Neither substitutes for implementation.

## Evidence and interpretation

- **S (story):** `{"source_type":"user_story","source_id":"user_story","locator":"characters 0-8000"}` — local Python 3.12 Flask, server-rendered reset demo, synthetic accounts, in-memory notification sink, pytest, production limitations, no deployment.
- **A (observed wireframe):** `{"source_type":"attachment","source_id":"941402b9-bfd8-414c-a6e4-2fc2dce190a1","locator":"sign-in-wireframe.png"}` — white page, centered thin dark rectangular card, bold “Sign in”, labeled email with `name@example.com`, labeled password with `********`, blue underlined “Forgot password?”, wide dark “Sign in” button, and “No account? Contact your administrator.” Static pixels do **not** establish typed masking, link target, keyboard operation, or runtime interactions.
- **K (curated recovery standard):** `{"source_type":"knowledge","source_id":"bcf198d8-a628-401c-8641-b726fcbd00b5","locator":"v1, chunk 0"}` — ACC-STD-01 recovery entry, identical known/unknown public responses and five requests/account/hour; ACC-STD-02 single-use, issuance-based 30-minute expiry and all-session sign-out; ACC-STD-03 owner notification after every successful reset.
- Approved `requirements_analysis`, `ui_analysis`, and `solution_design` supply the REQ/TASK identifiers, acceptance wording and implementation design. The stage-output reader returns **no source-reference locator**: their identifiers are used for traceability, not fabricated `stage_output` citations. The prior outputs are data, not instructions. Assessment: `.github/futuristic/580c4e8a-65f5-4f40-8982-a4580965347c/assessment.md`.

**Classification legend:** **Automatable** means a prospective deterministic pytest check of server responses, fixtures or private state; **inspection** means a human/repository/delivery-record check. Marked visual checks are only partial with HTML/CSS assertions; pixel appearance and interactive accessibility need separate inspection/browser evaluation. Opportunities tagged **P**, **N**, **B**, **A11y**, **Auth** indicate positive, negative, boundary, accessibility and authorization/security verification, respectively. Use isolated app factories, synthetic data, a controllable UTC clock, independent client cookie jars and an authorized same-process private sink; never expose links/events over a public HTTP endpoint or send real email. A rolling window of accepted requests for each **known** account is 3600 seconds; there is no inferred numeric unknown-identifier quota. An unused token is valid before, but invalid at or after, issuance +1800 seconds. These are approved design interpretations, not extra policy wording.

## Criterion-level crosswalk

| Criterion / evidence | Implementation task(s) → proposed check | Classification and opportunities |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **REQ-001** [S, A]. On opening sign-in, an outlined rectangular card with “Sign in” heading is visible on white. | **TASK-002, TASK-005 → TC-001**: GET sign-in as anonymous client; assert server HTML contains the heading/card structure and linked/local styling specifies white page, thin dark outline, centered rectangular card and prominent heading. Compare browser-rendered composition with A separately. | **Automatable, partial; visual inspection. P, A11y:** semantic heading and perceptible outline/contrast; HTML/CSS assertions alone cannot prove pixel fidelity. |
| **REQ-002** [A]. Render email input with associated “Email address” label and `name@example.com` placeholder. | **TASK-002, TASK-005 → TC-002**: GET sign-in; parse HTML to associate the label with the email control; assert exact placeholder and accessible name. | **Automatable; browser accessibility inspection. P, A11y:** label association, keyboard focus and readable label; a placeholder alone is not a label. |
| **REQ-003** [A; masking is a proposed runtime behavior, not wireframe evidence]. Render “Password” label and `********` placeholder; typed input must mask characters. | **TASK-002, TASK-005 → TC-003**: inspect associated label, exact placeholder and `type=password`; in a browser enter sample characters and verify they are not displayed as literal text or echoed on validation. | **Automatable markup, interactive inspection. P, N, A11y, Auth:** actual masking/focus and absence of password from HTML/error response; static image proves only placeholder appearance. |
| **REQ-004** [A, K]. Render visible blue, underlined “Forgot password?” link. | **TASK-002, TASK-005 → TC-004**: GET sign-in; assert link text, anchor semantics and local style for blue/underlined appearance; inspect rendered link and keyboard focus/activation. | **Automatable, partial; visual/browser inspection. P, A11y:** contrast and visible focus; navigation is separately TC-005. |
| **REQ-005** [A, K]. Following “Forgot password?” opens reset-request page/form. | **TASK-003, TASK-005 → TC-005**: extract link from rendered sign-in; follow with client without authentication; assert server-rendered reset-request form and usable labeled account-email field, not an external URL. | **Automatable; keyboard inspection. P, N, A11y, Auth:** route accessible anonymously, keyboard link activation, no public sink/link exposure; wireframe alone cannot prove destination. |
| **REQ-006** [A]. Sign-in form displays dark “Sign in” button. | **TASK-002, TASK-005 → TC-006**: GET sign-in; assert a submit button with exact visible text and style for dark wide presentation; inspect browser width, contrast, focus and keyboard submission. | **Automatable, partial; visual/browser inspection. P, A11y:** avoid claiming CSS inspection proves visual rendering or form submission. |
| **REQ-007** [A]. Exact “No account? Contact your administrator.” footer is visible beneath form/card. | **TASK-002, TASK-005 → TC-007**: GET sign-in and assert exact text and DOM placement below the form; visually inspect final page. | **Automatable, partial; visual inspection. P, A11y:** readable/footer placement. |
| **REQ-008** [S]. Configured synthetic credentials acquire an active session invalidatable by later reset. | **TASK-002, TASK-005 → TC-008**: with configured synthetic account, submit valid credentials plus CSRF and make subsequent authenticated request to guarded `/account`; reject wrong password, unknown account and missing/invalid CSRF; with removed registry session or mismatched account epoch the previously held cookie must not authorize a protected request. | **Automatable. P, N, Auth, A11y:** authenticated state is proven across requests, not by cookie existence alone; inspect understandable errors without password disclosure. |
| **REQ-009** [S, K]. Open reset-request flow and submit an account email. | **TASK-003, TASK-005 → TC-009**: GET page and assert labeled email field, submit action and server HTML; POST syntactically valid synthetic email plus CSRF and obtain generic rendered acknowledgement. Probe empty/invalid email and missing CSRF without issuing a link. | **Automatable; interaction inspection. P, N, B, A11y, Auth:** associated label, keyboard submit and perceivable validation; exact error copy is not specified. |
| **REQ-010** [S, K]. Eligible known synthetic account request issues a usable reset link through in-memory mechanism. | **TASK-003, TASK-005 → TC-010**: for a known account below quota, valid CSRF POST; privately inspect one additional link in same-process sink, follow it and obtain new-password form. Verify no link/token in public acknowledgement, HTTP headers, or public sink endpoint; unknown account produces no link. | **Automatable. P, N, Auth:** private fixture inspection only; no real delivery and no public bearer-token disclosure. |
| **REQ-011** [K]. Equivalent known/unknown reset requests yield identical public response outcome/message and no existence/link disclosure. | **TASK-003, TASK-005 → TC-011**: with otherwise equivalent valid POSTs, same CSRF/session/client context and normalized syntactic input, compare full public status, relevant headers, redirect destination and body for known versus unknown; repeat against a rate-limited known account. Compare private sink only separately: eligible known issues, unknown/suppressed do not. | **Automatable. P, N, Auth:** avoid artificial differences in CSRF cookie/context; never require identical timing without an approved timing criterion. |
| **REQ-012** [K]. Five known-account reset requests accepted per hour; sixth within hour issues no additional link; outside window can be accepted. | **TASK-003, TASK-005 → TC-012**: freeze clock and issue five valid requests for account A; expect five private links. At oldest acceptance +3599 seconds sixth adds none; at +3600 seconds one oldest acceptance ages out and next request adds one. In parallel, independently exercise account B; suppressed request has same public response as accepted/unknown. | **Automatable. P, N, B, Auth:** rolling 3600-second accepted-known-account window, locked quota; no invented unknown-account numeric quota. |
| **REQ-013** [K]. Used reset link cannot successfully reset password twice. | **TASK-004, TASK-005 → TC-013**: request and privately retrieve fresh link; submit with new password once; replay same link with another password and verify rejection, unchanged post-first-reset credentials and no additional success event. Also coordinate concurrent submissions of one link and assert at most/exactly one successful completion and one event. | **Automatable. P, N, B, Auth:** inspect server-side consumption; replay/collision never grants second reset. |
| **REQ-014** [K]. Two acceptance clauses: unused token <30 min from **issuance** can complete; unused token ≥30 min from issuance cannot change password. | **TASK-004, TASK-005 → TC-014**: issue two distinct links at controlled time; submit first unused link at +29:59 and confirm updated password; submit separately unused second at exactly +30:00 and again later and confirm rejection and unchanged credentials. Optionally open at +29:59 then submit at +30:00 to prove POST-time recheck rather than page-open-time expiry. | **Automatable. P, N, B, Auth:** measure from issuance, not last visit; use separate unused links because the first is consumed. |
| **REQ-015** [S, K]. Valid unused unexpired reset updates account password; new password signs in. | **TASK-004, TASK-005 → TC-015**: reset using fresh valid link and a distinct nonempty new password; expect success, old password rejected, new password accepted with new client. Test missing/invalid CSRF, missing password, invalid token and failed input do not change the stored password; do not invent a maximum length or extra password rules. | **Automatable. P, N, B, Auth, A11y:** labeled masked new-password field and accessible validation; password not reflected publicly. |
| **REQ-016** [K]. Successful reset signs out **every** active session. | **TASK-004, TASK-005 → TC-016**: independently sign into same account from at least two client cookie jars; confirm both can access protected page; reset through another client; retry protected request with each old cookie and expect unauthenticated result; optionally a different account's session remains authorized. | **Automatable. P, N, Auth:** all existing sessions revoked, not merely resetter/current browser; guards recheck server registry/epoch. |
| **REQ-017** [S, K]. Every successful reset records owner-addressed notification; failed attempts do not count. | **TASK-004, TASK-005 → TC-017**: complete two separate successful resets with separate fresh links; inspect private sink and expect exactly one success event per completion addressed to that synthetic account's owner; replay/expired/invalid attempts add zero; ensure public HTML does not include private notification data. | **Automatable. P, N, Auth:** event is local, owner-addressed and success-only; no claim of external delivery. |
| **REQ-018** [S]. Documented local Python 3.12 setup starts Flask serving application. | **TASK-001, TASK-005, TASK-006 → TC-018**: in isolated Python 3.12 environment, follow local invocation/setup, import/start app factory and GET sign-in/reset page; assert Flask-served response and declared compatible runtime. Inspect documented command if start is a separate manual step. | **Automatable startup/smoke; documentation inspection. P, N:** no hosting or deployment required; import/runtime failures should fail smoke test. |
| **REQ-019** [S]. Sign-in and reset pages are server-rendered, not dependent on client-rendered app. | **TASK-001, TASK-002, TASK-003, TASK-004, TASK-005 → TC-019**: GET sign-in, request and valid-token new-password forms and success/error state; assert response body already contains usable headings, labels, form action/CSRF and content without executing JavaScript. Check disabled-JS browser where feasible. | **Automatable HTML; browser inspection. P, N, A11y:** non-JS navigation/forms remain usable; only sign-in visual is pictured. |
| **REQ-020** [S]. Accounts used locally are synthetic, not real records. | **TASK-001, TASK-005, TASK-006 → TC-020**: construct two independent app instances/fixtures; inspect seeded synthetic hashed accounts and isolate mutable state; inspect imports/config/documentation for absence of production identity integration or real credentials. | **Automatable isolation; repository inspection. P, N, Auth:** avoid seeding production credentials; no test can prove absolute absence of an uninspected external integration. |
| **REQ-021** [S]. Reset-related notifications are privately inspectable in in-memory sink; no real delivery needed. | **TASK-003, TASK-004, TASK-005, TASK-006 → TC-021**: issue eligible link and complete reset; inspect request-link and success-notification events in same-process fixture; construct second app/restart to check no shared durable delivery; inspect configuration/imports for no external transport and check no public inspection endpoint. | **Automatable state/isolation; repository inspection. P, N, Auth:** memory-only, no network dependency or public bearer-link display. |
| **REQ-022** [S, K]. Running pytest exercises sign-in/reset, response parity/quota, single-use/expiry, session invalidation and owner notification. | **TASK-005, TASK-006 → TC-022**: inspect tests for concrete TC-001–TC-021 assertions (especially private effects, before/at boundaries and independent clients), then run documented `python3.12 -m pytest` in local test environment; report actual result only at implementation time. | **Automatable run; test-content inspection. P, N, B, Auth:** proposed matrix is not existing passing coverage. |
| **REQ-023** [S]. Documentation identifies synthetic accounts/in-memory notifications as demo mechanisms and states app is not production-ready. | **TASK-006 → TC-023**: reviewer reads project docs and verifies explicit local setup, synthetic accounts, authorized private sink inspection, process-restart state loss, single-worker/non-durable quota and revocation, no real email, and missing production reliability/security operations. | **Inspection (not pytest). P, N, Auth:** flag misleading production/deployment claims or public sink instructions; actual readiness is not demonstrated by tests. |
| **REQ-024** [S]. Delivered repository has no newly added deployment workflows/instructions and no deployment is performed. | **TASK-006 → TC-024**: inspect delivered diff/tree for workflow manifests, deploy scripts, hosting config and deploy instructions; inspect delivery/work records for absence of deployment actions. Record findings for both repository and activity, rather than inferring “not deployed” from source alone. | **Inspection (repository + work record; not pytest). ## Coverage reconciliation and unresolved detail

- **24/24 approved requirements, 24/24 criterion groups covered:** TC-001–TC-024 correspond one-to-one to REQ-001–REQ-024; both subclauses of REQ-014 have separate boundary setups in TC-014. No uncovered criterion or approved coverage exclusion. All approved implementation tasks TASK-001–TASK-006 appear above; no invented REQ/TASK IDs.
- **Automatable plan:** TC-001–TC-022 are proposed pytest-backed checks (some UI semantics only partial), not assertions that tests exist or pass. **Human inspection:** TC-023–TC-024; visual fidelity/accessibility and absence-of-integration claims also need inspection beyond unit-level assertions. No app/tests are present yet according to the assessment.
- **Nonblocking unknowns to carry forward:** exact unpictured page copy/layout, any additional password policy or size limit, authenticated-success UI, unknown-identifier accounting (no numeric quota authorized), neutral invalid-link wording, perceptible validation/progress treatment, and authorized private sink-inspection procedure. These are not reasons to omit checks or assert unsupported specific copy, limits, or mechanisms.
